title: Reduce GPU runtime probe latency and pin toolchain for deterministic kernel selection
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Our runtime currently performs a per-process runtime probe that inspects driver/kernel symbols, queries Triton/CUTLASS versions, and compiles or selects kernels at worker startup. This probe path can add 30-120ms to cold-starts for many workloads, and the nondeterministic ordering of symbol resolution has caused flakies when rolling kernel updates across heterogeneous fleets. In addition, small differences in the CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS toolchain between build agents lead to non-reproducible kernel blobs, making rollbacks and binary compatibility harder.

Goal: Reduce probe overhead on warm/cold starts by introducing a pre-warmable probe-cache and a deterministic toolchain lockfile that ensures identical kernel selection and packaging across CI/ops. Provide fallback semantics so older workers can still serve while a rollout happens, and add a CI regression harness to validate quantized and FP16 kernel parity across representative GPUs (A100/H100/T4).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Median probe latency for a worker process reduced to <10ms on warm start and <70ms on cold start in our standard A/B benchmark. 2) CI produces a deterministic kernel artifact hash (sha256) given the same toolchain lockfile across three build agents. 3) Rolling update test: at 0,25,50,75,100% rollout we show no increased error-rate >0.2% or token-latency regressions beyond SLA thresholds. 4) Regression harness validates quantized kernel output tolerance within configured thresholds for 99% of sampled prompts.
technical_notes:
Planned changes:
- Introduce a persistent probe-cache service (gRPC) that stores per-machine ABI/capability fingerprints and the precomputed kernel selection map. Worker process probes query the local cache agent before performing expensive symbol/version scans.
- Add a toolchain lockfile (toolchain.lock) that pins CUDA, Triton, CUTLASS commits + compiler flags, and a build-time kernel-abi manifest. Add verification step in CI that fails the build if produced kernel blobs differ from the manifest.
- Add an optional --skip-probe flag for controlled experiments; default behavior will be to consult probe-cache and fall back to full probe on cache-miss.
- Implement safe fallback: if a worker detects a toolchain mismatch against probe-cache-suggested kernels, it will attempt to use prebuilt compatible kernels from /opt/redwood/kernels/compat/ before recompiling.
- Add upstream CI job matrix: GPUs=[A100,H100,T4], precisions=[fp32,fp16,int8], Triton branches=[main,release-2.x], validating numerical parity and artifact hashes.

Implementation risks & mitigations:
- Stale cache entries causing incorrect kernel selection: include entry TTL and automatic reprobing upon mismatch, with detailed telemetry for fast diagnosis.
- Locking the toolchain could slow adoption of security updates: add an automated monthly bump job and highlight security fixes in the lockfile PR process.
- Increased storage for prebuilt kernels: cap kept artifacts per model/arch/precision to most-used families and add eviction policy.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Canary (week 1): Deploy probe-cache agent to 5% of Dedicated workers; enable --skip-probe for a subset of requests; collect latency and error telemetry. Phase 2 - Gradual (week 2-3): Enable probe-cache lookup by default for Dedicated and Hosted warm pools; populate prebuilt kernel store for top 30 models. Phase 3 - Fleet Roll (week 4): Release toolchain.lock enforcement for builds and enable deterministic artifact verification in CI. Monitor rollback automation and tracer spikes. Final: Flip default to use probe-cache on all environments once stability confirmed.
